column41: UNICADO is a large framework. It's basic and general understand of how it works at a surface level is only ever introduced briefly in courses such as Aircraft Design Basics (which is the only one I have attended so far at this time of the survey). In Aircraft Design Basics, most, but not all, aircraft design concepts are implemented into the UNICADO Framework. For example, this mentioned lecture is divided into topics that correspond to the different modules in the UNICADO Framework (Propulsion Design topic -> Propulsion Design Module). In the propulsion design topic of the lecture, it is not clear nor is it shown how the introduced theory is implemented for sizing calculations and methods. Additionally, it does not show its dependency on obtaining upstream parameters from other modules (consequently corresponding to other topics in the lecture before / after it), which is critical to understand how the different modules (topics of the Aircraft Design Basics lecture) work all together; this is only briefly mentioned in the introduction and ending. It would take more than an entire lecture to understand the workings of its entirety, its workflow, and its purposes.

The main challenges I selected above can be summarized into 3 critical areas:
1. Difficulty in the installation and set-up due to lack of proper guidance (which depend on the level of the user's software / computer knowledge),
2. Lack of tutorials on how to begin with the entire UNICADO Framework or individual modules of the UNICADO Framework (which depend on the user's purpose for using UNICADO),
3. Lack of visualization for documentation on how the entire framework is structured, what workflows in the framework are available, how the workflows in the framework look like / perform, what parameters (global / local inputs and outputs) flow through the framework / workflow, and how these parameters are obtained, processed as well as transferred.

column48:
When a user (especially a student) has the goal or task which requires utilizing UNICADO, where they begin depends entirely on their capabilities. Even with the clear start of requiring to install and set up UNICADO, they would require a certain programing knowledge to facilitate them in setting up and dealing with installation errors. It is also unclear at time where they should start. Should they start with a tutorial? Should they look at a workflow example? Do they have sufficient theory knowledge to understand a specific module and such would require them to learn that first before dealing with that module? Should they understand a specific programing language before hand when dealing with a source code or an entire module or the entire framework?
As one can see, the questions represent starting points depending on a user's current capabilities. Perhaps a short survey which asses this could be developed in a way that it outputs areas in which they must obtain knowledge in first. Perhaps AI could be integrated or coupled to the UNICADO's Framework / Definition / Workings in such a way that it would also be able to suggest how the user can proceed.
